title: AI Decisions
description: Configure the AI services used to classify data without traditional training, create new variables, and compare results with supervised models.

benchmark.title: Compare a zero-shot model
benchmark.description: Evaluate a fixed question with a dataset that already has correct answers. The outcome column is used only for local metrics and is never sent to the external service.
benchmark.targetHelp: Profile suggestions appear first, but any classification column with every class identified can be used.
benchmark.inputs: Data sent to the external service
benchmark.targetExcluded: The outcome column and every unselected column are excluded from external requests.
benchmark.question: Question the model should answer
benchmark.externalAck: I understand that the selected columns will be processed by the configured external service.
benchmark.error: The comparison could not be started. Review the fields, test the connection, and try again.
benchmark.historyError: Previous comparisons could not be loaded.
benchmark.noRunsDescription: Configure the comparison above and start a run to see results here.
benchmark.finalizing: All rows have been processed; finalizing calibration.
benchmark.progressHelp: Progress updates automatically; select the comparison to view calibration.

comparison.title: Same-sample comparison
comparison.supervisedDescription: Models trained with known answers, such as CatBoost, XGBoost, and Random Forest.
comparison.zeroShotDescription: Jev answers directly without training on this dataset, using Noul or Choice questions.
comparison.tooltip: These approaches use different training conditions and should not be interpreted as a like-for-like model leaderboard.
comparison.pairedTooltip: The metrics below use the exact same evaluation rows, but supervised training and zero-shot remain different methodologies.
comparison.noCompatibleExperiments: No completed supervised experiment has the same dataset, target, and task.
comparison.error: These runs could not be compared.
comparison.noPersistedPredictions: The selected experiment predates the comparison contract. Run it again to persist validation predictions.

help.title: Compares each supervised model and the zero-shot model on the exact same rows. This reduces sample bias but does not make their training methods equivalent.
help.accuracy: Overall proportion of correct predictions. Higher is better, but it can hide poor performance on rare classes.
help.f1: Balances precision and recall. Higher is better; it is useful when both error types have similar importance.
help.rocAuc: Measures how well positives rank above negatives across thresholds. Higher is better.
help.prAuc: Summarizes precision and recall across thresholds. Higher is better and it is more informative than ROC-AUC for imbalanced classes.
help.brier: Squared error of predicted probabilities. Lower is better; it evaluates correctness and calibration together.
help.ece: Average gap between predicted confidence and observed accuracy. Lower is better.
help.latency: 95th percentile of real provider-call latency. Cache hits are excluded.
help.cost: Estimated cost for the shared rows. It is unavailable for older artifacts without per-row usage.
help.delta: Δ = supervised minus zero-shot. Positive values favor supervised for higher-is-better metrics; negative values favor supervised for Brier and ECE.

calibration.title: Calibration Lab
calibration.error: Calibration results could not be loaded.
calibration.errorDescription: Try loading again, or return to history and choose another comparison.
calibration.processing: The zero-shot benchmark is still processing.
calibration.interrupted: The comparison stopped because the server restarted. Start a new comparison.
calibration.persistedOnly: Threshold exploration uses persisted probabilities and does not call the Decision Provider again.
calibration.noProviderLatency: This run has no real provider calls; every response came from cache.

help.brier: Measures squared probability error. Zero is perfect; lower values mean more accurate and better-calibrated probabilities.
help.logLoss: Penalizes incorrect probabilities, especially confident mistakes. Lower is better.
help.ece: Compares predicted confidence with observed accuracy across bins. Lower is better; zero means perfect calibration on this sample.
help.latencyP95: 95% of real provider calls completed within this time. Cache hits are excluded.
help.providerCalls: Number of rows that required a real provider call in this run.
help.cacheHits: Responses reused from cache without another provider call.
help.runCost: Sum of the estimated cost reported by the provider for the full run.
help.threshold: Predictions at or above the threshold are automated; the remaining predictions are not automated.
help.coverage: Share of samples whose confidence reaches the threshold and can be automated.
help.accuracy: Accuracy among only the samples covered by the current threshold.
help.reviewRate: Share below the current threshold. It may require human review, abstention, or another downstream policy.
help.reliability: Compare observed accuracy with the ideal diagonal. The closer the curve is to the diagonal, the better calibrated the probabilities are.
help.histogram: Shows where confidence values are concentrated. High bars near 1 mean many confident predictions, not necessarily correct ones.
help.thresholdChart: Shows the tradeoff between automating more cases and retaining accuracy. Raising the threshold usually reduces coverage and may increase accuracy.
help.latency: Distribution of real provider calls only. Use it to identify variability and latency tails; cache hits are excluded.

semantic.title: Create variables with AI
semantic.description: Turn free text or text columns you choose into reviewable numeric variables and measure their impact on a supervised model.
semantic.flowHelp: Flow: select text columns → review suggested questions → generate variables → open the set in history. Training comparison is optional and requires selecting an experiment before generation.
semantic.discover: Define what to extract from the text
semantic.textColumnsHelp: Only checked columns may be sampled for proposal and sent during generation.
semantic.optionalWarning: Categorical values may already help the model without AI. Select only columns available at prediction time; avoid personal data, the target, and information known only after the outcome.
semantic.noTextColumns: This dataset has no eligible text columns for semantic generation.
semantic.costUnavailable: Token and cost estimates are unavailable until the provider reports usage.
semantic.questionTypesHelp: Noul: Binary yes/no question producing 1 probability feature. Choice: Categorical question producing 1 probability feature per option. Score: Ordered scale producing expected score and uncertainty.

typeHelp.noul: Binary yes/no question. The Decision Model evaluates each row and generates 1 column with the predicted probability (0.0 to 1.0).
typeHelp.choice: Classification across 2 or more mutually exclusive alternatives. The Decision Model generates 1 probability column per option.
typeHelp.score: Ordered scale from 2 to 10 levels. The Decision Model generates 2 columns: expected score and uncertainty.

semantic.newQuestion: Does this text contain the semantic signal?
semantic.question: Question
semantic.invalidCriteria: Use valid criteria for this question type.
semantic.noImpact: Do not run supervised impact comparison
semantic.externalAck: I understand that only the selected columns will be processed by the configured external Decision Provider.
semantic.cancelError: Could not cancel generation. Try again.
semantic.queuedNextStep: Follow the highlighted card in the history below.
semantic.error: The semantic variable request could not be completed. Review the questions and try again.
semantic.historyError: Previously generated variables could not be loaded.
semantic.emptyDescription: Define and review the questions above to generate the first set.
semantic.waitingForWorker: Waiting for variable generation to start
semantic.finalizing: All rows have been processed; finalizing the results and optional comparison.
semantic.progressHelp: Progress updates automatically; open the set details to see the questions and output file.
semantic.impactAvailable: Comparison with experiment {{experiment}} is complete. The table shows the observed numerical change after adding variables; this does not prove a generalizable gain.
semantic.noImpactAvailable: Variables were generated, but no training comparison ran because no experiment was selected before generation. This set therefore does not yet demonstrate a training gain. To measure impact in a new run, select a completed experiment during review.
semantic.impactUnavailable: Variables were generated, but no comparison results are available for this set.
semantic.generationFailed: Generation failed; do not use this set as a completed result.
semantic.questionsFrozenHelp: These are the questions used for this run. The selected decision model applied them to dataset rows; they cannot be edited in this set.
semantic.outputFileHelp: Parquet in local artifact storage; with default Docker Compose, the path below is inside data/experiments/. The file is not automatically added to new training runs.
semantic.deltaVsTfidfHelp: Metric with JEV variables minus the metric with local TF-IDF. Interpret the sign using metric direction; it is not a statistical significance measure.
semantic.comparisonTitle: Impact of semantic variables on training
semantic.comparisonHelp: Two fresh evaluations of the same experiment: one with the original variables and one with the original plus variables generated by the configured Decision Provider (such as JEV). Other parameters and validation are the same.
semantic.comparisonHelpThreeArms: Three evaluations with the same folds and models: original variables, originals plus local text TF-IDF, and originals plus JEV semantic variables. TF-IDF is fitted only on each training fold. The difference does not prove causality.
semantic.noLocalTextBaseline: The additional TF-IDF arm was not available in this evaluation. It requires new free-text input relative to the original experiment and compatible models; the JEV result remains available without it. Review the columns used.
semantic.noShap: No semantic variable appears in the available SHAP summary.
semantic.comparisonCaution: Confirm every input column existed at prediction time. The observed difference does not prove causality or statistical significance; SHAP does not prove metric improvement.
semantic.baselineHelp: Metric value after retraining with original variables. This is not necessarily the selected experiment's historical result.
semantic.augmentedHelp: Value after retraining with the same settings plus semantic variables.
semantic.deltaHelp: Value with JEV minus value without JEV. Interpret its sign using the metric's direction.
semantic.percentHelp: Delta divided by the absolute value without JEV. This is a relative change, not statistical certainty.
semantic.directionHelp: Some metrics should increase, such as ROC AUC; others should decrease, such as RMSE.
semantic.evaluationTimeHelp: Duration of the displayed evaluations, including explainability in the JEV arm. It is not the additional time spent generating JEV variables.
semantic.shapHelp: Semantic-variable importance in the JEV-augmented model's SHAP analysis. Importance does not imply improvement or causality.
semantic.aiUnavailable: Configure an explanation model to use this option.

cascade.title: Set a confidence policy
cascade.description: Simulate which predictions would be accepted automatically, sent for human review, or left undecided without calling the model again.
cascade.error: The policy could not be simulated. Review the thresholds and try again.
cascade.persistedOnly: Threshold exploration uses persisted benchmark outputs and never calls the Decision Provider.
cascade.historyError: Confidence policies could not be loaded.
cascade.emptyDescription: Select a completed comparison above and simulate the first policy.

help.sourceRun: Completed benchmark whose persisted probabilities will be used in the simulation. No new provider call is made.
help.autoThreshold: Minimum confidence required to accept a prediction automatically.
help.reviewThreshold: Samples between this value and the automatic threshold go to review. Below it, the low-confidence action is applied.
help.lowConfidenceAction: Controls whether cases below the review threshold receive manual review or abstention.
help.reviewCost: Estimated cost per item sent to human review. It is added to the provider cost already incurred.
help.exploreThreshold: Changes the automatic threshold locally without saving another run or calling the provider.
help.coverage: Share accepted automatically by the policy at the current threshold.
help.accuracy: Accuracy calculated only among automatically accepted decisions.
help.errorRate: Error share among automatic decisions. Lower is better.
help.reviewRate: Share sent to human review by the policy.
help.abstainRate: Share for which the policy makes no decision and returns an abstention.
help.cost: Provider cost plus the estimated cost of manual reviews.
help.thresholdChart: Shows how coverage, accuracy, error, review, abstention, and cost change as the automatic threshold moves.
help.distribution: Shows how many samples fall into each confidence range and helps estimate the impact of moving thresholds.
